title: In situ Temperature and Beam-Driven Relaxation Dynamics by Electron Time Correlation Microscopy (EtCM)
content: Amorphous matter typically shows a distribution of atomic bonding energies and corresponding local structures. Related to that, atomic jump frequencies show a broad distribution of thermal activation and corresponding time scales. Thus, already at room temperature and enhanced by the electron beam, the dynamics of an amorphous structure or glass is active. In the present work, in situ beam driven and in situ heating experiments were conducted to elucidate the structure and dynamics of various amorphous structures.
